theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Breakfast starts soon at a villa. What should you do first at the beverage station?
options: Wait for the first order before you switch on any equipment
Check the equipment works and stock up cups, milk, sugar and coffee
Pour coffee into every cup now so that guests are served at once
Leave the cleaning of the station until after breakfast is over

Putting the station away neatly once the service has ended
Placing a drinks menu card on each table before guests arrive
Making a list of the drinks that guests ordered the day before

options: In front of the older cartons, so that they are used first
On top of the pile, so staff take whichever they reach first
Behind the older cartons, so the older stock is used first

questions.stem: Mrs Campbell orders coffee for six people at 8:00 a.m. When is the best time to brew it?

The night before, then kept in the fridge until the morning
An hour early, then left standing on the hot plate until needed
Only after the guests have finished eating their main meal

questions.stem: Which piece of equipment do you use to make a fruit smoothie?

A glass holds too little ice, so serving drinks takes longer
A metal scoop keeps the ice colder than a glass can
A glass makes the ice melt faster and the drinks go weak

options: Pick out the pieces of glass you can see and keep using the ice
Leave it, because the glass will sink to the bottom of the bin
Empty the bin, melt the ice away, clean it and refill it

Evaporated milk from a tin

Espresso topped up with hot water to make a long black coffee

Wipe it with a clean damp cloth and purge a short burst of steam

questions.stem: How should freshly squeezed orange juice be stored until service?

In a closed jug beside the warm coffee machine
In the ice bin, poured straight over the ice

questions.stem: What is a "mocktail"?

questions.stem: When should a sealed bottle of water be opened for a guest?

questions.stem: From which side are drinks normally served to a seated guest?
options: From the left, with the left hand
From behind, over the shoulder
From the right, with the right hand

questions.stem: How should you hold a glass when you serve it?
options: By the rim, so you can carry several
Inside the glass, with fingers spread

On the palm, with heavy items near your body

questions.stem: A villa guest asks for "coffee, black, no sugar". What should you do before you serve it?
options: Add milk anyway, as most guests take it
Bring sugar too, and add it if they look unhappy

questions.stem: Hot drinks should be served in cups that are:
options: Taken straight from the fridge
Still wet from the dishwasher
Chipped but clean

questions.stem: A guest complains that her tea is cold. What is the best response?
options: Tell her the tea was hot when you brought it out

What do you call coffee that has had most of its caffeine taken out?

Which gas makes soft drinks and soda water fizzy?

When a cup of tea or coffee is set down for a guest, its handle points to which side?

essays.stem: A villa party of eight will have breakfast on the verandah at 8:00 a.m. Describe how you would plan and set up the beverage station before they come.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the guest list and any special requests, such as decaf coffee, plant milk or no sugar, and find out how many guests will come. I switch on the coffee machine and kettle in good time and check that they work and are clean. I stock the station with enough cups, saucers, glasses, teaspoons, napkins and trays for eight guests and some spare. I fill the sugar bowls and sweetener, put milk in clean jugs and keep it in the fridge until it is needed. I squeeze or prepare the juice, cover it, label and date it and chill it at 5 °C or below. I fill the ice bin with a scoop beside it. Tea, herbal teas and local chocolate are set out with lemon slices. I brew the coffee just before 8:00 so that it is fresh. Finally I check that the area is tidy and safe, with no trailing cables or wet floors.
markingPoints: Checks numbers and special requests or dietary needs
Switches on and checks equipment in good time
Stocks enough cups, glasses, cutlery, sugar and milk
Prepares and chills juice and ice safely (covered, labelled, 5 °C or below)
Times the brewing so drinks are fresh; leaves the station tidy and safe

essays.stem: Explain, step by step, how you would make and serve a cappuccino with an espresso machine.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with a warm, clean cup. I remove the portafilter, wipe it dry, and fill the basket with freshly ground fine coffee, the amount the machine's guide gives. I level it and tamp it firmly and evenly with the tamper. I flush the group head briefly, lock the portafilter in and start the shot straight away. A good shot takes about 25 to 30 seconds and has a golden-brown crema. While it runs I fill the milk jug about a third full with cold milk, purge the steam wand, and steam the milk, letting in air at the start to make foam. I stop before the milk boils, when the jug is hot to hold. I tap and swirl the jug, then pour the milk onto the espresso, finishing with a thick layer of foam. I wipe and purge the steam wand at once. I serve the cup on a saucer with a teaspoon from the guest's right, with the handle to the right, and offer sugar.
markingPoints: Warm cup; dose, level and tamp fine ground coffee correctly
Pulls the shot in about 25–30 seconds with crema
Steams cold milk to make foam without boiling it
Pours steamed milk with a thick layer of foam on top
Wipes and purges the wand; serves correctly with saucer, spoon and sugar

essays.stem: Describe how to make and serve a pot of black tea for two guests, and say how making green tea and herbal tea is different.
essays.modelAnswer: I fill the kettle with fresh cold water and bring it to the boil. While it heats, I warm the teapot with a little hot water and pour it away. I put in the tea leaves or tea bags, about one bag or one teaspoon for each cup, and pour on water that has just boiled. I let the tea brew for about 3 to 5 minutes. I set a tray with two cups and saucers, teaspoons, a milk jug, sugar bowl, lemon slices and a jug of hot water to top up the pot. I serve from the guest's right and tell them the tea is ready to pour. Green tea is different because boiling water makes it bitter: I use water just off the boil, about 70 to 80 °C, and brew it for a shorter time, about 2 to 3 minutes. Herbal or bush teas such as fever grass, mint or ginger use boiling water and can be left to steep for longer, about 5 minutes or more.
markingPoints: Fresh water, freshly boiled; warms the pot first
Correct amount of tea and brewing time of about 3–5 minutes
Tray set with cups, saucers, spoons, milk, sugar, lemon and hot water
Green tea: cooler water (about 70–80 °C) and a shorter time
Herbal tea: boiling water and a longer steep

essays.stem: Explain the food safety rules you follow when you prepare and store fresh juice, milk and ice.
essays.modelAnswer: I wash my hands before I start and wear a clean uniform with my hair tied back. I hold a Food Handler's Permit from the local health department. I wash all fruit in clean water before cutting it, using a clean board and knife kept for fruit. I squeeze or blend only what I need for the service. Fresh juice and milk are high-risk because germs grow fast in them when they are warm. I keep them covered, labelled with the date and time, in a fridge at 5 °C or below, or as the Centre's food safety plan says, and I use the oldest stock first. I throw away juice or milk past its time or that smells or looks wrong. Ice is food too: I take it only with a clean scoop, never with a glass or my hands, and keep the scoop outside the ice. If a glass breaks near the ice, I empty the bin, clean it and refill it.
markingPoints: Hand washing, clean uniform and a Food Handler's Permit
Washes fruit; uses clean boards and knives
Covers, labels, dates and chills at 5 °C or below (or as the food safety plan says)
Rotates stock (oldest first) and discards out-of-date or spoiled drinks
Ice handled with a scoop only; empties the bin if glass breaks

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare and serve a fruit mocktail for a guest, such as a Jamaican fruit punch made without alcohol.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the recipe and ask the guest about any allergies. I wash my hands and get my equipment ready: a jigger or measuring cup, a blender or shaker, an ice scoop, a highball or hurricane glass and the garnish. I wash and cut the fruit, such as pineapple, orange and watermelon, on a clean board. I measure each juice and the syrup into the shaker or blender, so that every drink tastes the same, then add ice and shake or blend it until it is cold and mixed. I fill a chilled glass with fresh ice using the scoop and strain or pour the drink over it. I add a garnish, such as a slice of orange and a cherry on a pick, and a straw. I put the glass on a coaster on a tray and serve it from the guest's right, holding it by the base. Last, I clean the equipment and wipe down the work area.
markingPoints: Checks the recipe and any allergies
Washes hands and fruit; prepares equipment and glass
Measures ingredients so the drink is the same each time
Uses fresh ice with a scoop; mixes and pours neatly
Garnishes and serves correctly (coaster, tray, from the right), then cleans up

essays.stem: Explain how you would clean the espresso machine and the blender at the end of the day, and how you stay safe while doing it.
essays.modelAnswer: For the espresso machine, I empty and rinse the drip tray and the used coffee grounds box. I take out the portafilter baskets, soak and wash them. I backflush the group heads with water, and with the cleaning product when the maker's instructions say, using a blind basket. I wipe the group seals with a brush. I purge the steam wand, wipe it, and soak the tip if milk has dried on it. I wipe the outside with a damp cloth. For the blender, I switch it off and unplug it first. I wash the jug and lid in warm soapy water, taking care with the sharp blades, rinse and leave them to dry. I wipe the motor base with a damp cloth but never put it in water. To stay safe I keep my hands away from steam and hot water, wear gloves for chemicals, read the label and safety data sheet, dilute products correctly and never mix them.
markingPoints: Empties drip tray and grounds box; washes portafilters and baskets
Backflushes the group heads as the maker's instructions say
Purges and cleans the steam wand
Unplugs the blender; washes jug and blades carefully; base never in water
Safety: care with steam, gloves, follows the label and SDS, never mixes chemicals

essays.stem: A guest tells you she is allergic to nuts and her husband has diabetes. Explain how you would serve their drinks safely.
essays.modelAnswer: I thank the guest for telling me and write the allergy and need on the order. I tell my supervisor and the kitchen or bar team. For the nut allergy, I check the labels of every product I use, such as syrups, plant milks and flavoured coffees, because almond milk and some syrups contain nuts. I use clean equipment, such as a washed blender jug and a clean spoon, so that no nut product from an earlier drink gets into hers. I do not guess: if I am not sure what is in a product, I tell her honestly and offer a drink I know is safe. For the guest with diabetes, I offer drinks with no added sugar, such as water, unsweetened tea or coffee with a sugar-free sweetener, and I tell him that fruit juice is high in natural sugar. I serve the right drink to the right person and confirm it as I put it down.
markingPoints: Records the need and tells the supervisor and team
Checks labels for nuts (for example almond milk, syrups)
Uses clean equipment to avoid cross-contact
Never guesses; offers a known-safe choice
Offers sugar-free or unsweetened choices; serves and confirms the right drink to the right guest

essays.stem: Describe how you would carry a tray of drinks to a table of four guests on the verandah and serve them correctly.
essays.modelAnswer: I use a clean tray with a non-slip mat or a damp cloth on it. I load the tray with the heavy and tall drinks near the centre and close to my body, so it is balanced. I carry it on the palm and fingers of my left hand at about waist height, keeping my right hand free, and I walk carefully, watching for steps and wet patches. At the table I go to each guest's right side. I put a coaster down first, then place the glass on it, holding it by the base or stem and never touching the rim. I place hot drinks with the handle to the guest's right. I serve ladies and older guests first, or follow the order the host prefers, and I say the name of each drink as I put it down. I ask if they need anything else, then leave quietly and keep an eye on the table so I can clear empty glasses.
markingPoints: Clean tray with a non-slip surface; loads heavy items to the centre
Carries on the palm at waist height, walks safely
Serves from the right; holds glasses by base or stem; uses coasters
Hot drink handles to the right; correct serving order; names each drink
Checks for further needs and clears empties

essays.stem: Compare filter coffee, French press coffee and espresso. Say how each is made, what grind it needs and how it usually tastes.
essays.modelAnswer: Filter coffee is made by pouring hot water over medium ground coffee in a paper or mesh filter, by hand or in a machine. The water drips through slowly, so the coffee is clean and light, with little sediment. A French press, or plunger pot, uses coarse ground coffee. The hot water and coffee stay together for about 4 minutes, and then the mesh plunger is pushed down to hold the grounds at the bottom. It gives a fuller, heavier coffee, with a little sediment in the cup. Espresso is made in a machine that forces hot water under pressure through fine ground coffee that has been tamped hard. It takes only about 25 to 30 seconds and makes a small, strong shot with a golden crema on top. Espresso is also the base for drinks such as cappuccino, latte and Americano.
markingPoints: Filter: hot water drips through medium grind; clean, light taste
French press: coarse grind, steeped about 4 minutes, plunger down
French press: fuller taste with some sediment
Espresso: fine, tamped coffee; water forced through under pressure
Espresso: small strong shot with crema in about 25–30 seconds; base for milk drinks

essays.stem: Explain the main hazards at a beverage station and what you do to control each one.
essays.modelAnswer: Hot water and steam from kettles, urns and the coffee machine can scald. I keep my hands away from the steam wand and group heads, pour hot water carefully and never fill kettles above the mark. Electricity is a hazard where there is water. I keep hands dry, check plugs and cables for damage before use, report faults and never use broken equipment. Broken glass can cut staff and get into ice or drinks. I use an ice scoop, throw away chipped glasses and empty the ice bin if glass breaks near it. Wet floors can cause slips. I wipe spills at once and put out a wet floor sign. Cleaning chemicals can burn skin and eyes, so I read the label and safety data sheet, wear gloves and never mix products. Blender blades can cut, so I unplug the blender before cleaning it. I follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules, and I report accidents to my supervisor.
markingPoints: Scalds from hot water and steam: care, never overfill, keep hands clear
Electricity: dry hands, check cables, report faults
Glass: ice scoop, discard chipped glass, empty ice bin if glass breaks
Wet floors: wipe at once, wet floor sign
Chemicals and blades: label, SDS, gloves, never mix; unplug before cleaning; report accidents

practical1.title: Set up and serve hot beverages for a villa breakfast
practical1.brief: Your group is the beverage team for a villa breakfast for six guests (the assessor and other trainees play the guests). Set up a clean, stocked beverage station. Then make and serve, to order: a pot of filter or French press coffee, a pot of black tea, a herbal (bush) tea such as fever grass or ginger, and a Jamaican chocolate tea. If the Centre has an espresso machine, also make at least two cappuccinos. Share the work so that every member brews at least one drink and serves at least one guest while the assessor watches: one member takes the orders and repeats them back, others brew, and others carry and serve. Each member also takes part in the clean-down. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the station is clean and the stock is put away.
materials: Kettle or urn, filter coffee machine or French press, and an espresso machine if the Centre has one
Ground coffee, black tea, a herbal tea (fever grass, mint or ginger), and local cocoa balls or chocolate
Milk, plant milk, sugar, sweetener and lemons
Teapots, milk jugs, sugar bowls, cups, saucers, teaspoons and trays
Order pad, coasters, napkins and clean cloths
Washing-up liquid, sanitiser, gloves and a wet floor sign
photos: The beverage station set up and stocked before service
Members washing hands and in clean uniform
The chocolate tea and herbal tea ready to serve
A tray set and carried correctly to the guests
Drinks placed for the guests, with cup handles to the right
The station cleaned down and stock put away
checklist: Arrived in clean uniform, hair tied back, and washed hands before starting
Checked the equipment and stocked the station before service
Took or confirmed an order clearly and repeated it back
Brewed at least one drink correctly (right water, amount and time)
Kept milk chilled and handled food and drink hygienically
Carried a tray safely and served from the guest's right, holding cups and glasses correctly
Worked safely with hot water, steam and electricity
Took part in cleaning the equipment and the station
safety: Keep hands clear of steam wands, kettles and hot water; never overfill a kettle or urn
Check plugs and cables before use; keep hands dry; report any fault and do not use the equipment
Wipe spills at once and put out a wet floor sign
Read the label and safety data sheet for cleaning products, wear gloves and never mix chemicals
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules for every machine

practical2.title: Prepare and serve fresh juices, a smoothie and a mocktail
practical2.brief: Your group runs a cold-drinks bar for a pool-side guest event at a villa. Prepare, from fresh fruit: one fresh juice (such as orange, June plum or carrot), one fruit smoothie, one mocktail (such as a fruit punch or a virgin piña colada) and a jug of iced tea or sorrel. Each drink must be measured, garnished and served in a suitable glass. Every member makes at least one drink from start to finish while the assessor watches, and every member serves at least one drink from a tray to a "guest" (the assessor or another trainee). Store any spare juice correctly, covered, labelled and dated in the fridge. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the bar is clean.
materials: Fresh fruit (for example oranges, pineapple, June plum, carrots, bananas, limes) and prepared sorrel or tea
Electric blender, juicer or citrus press, measuring jug and jigger
Ice, ice bin and ice scoop
Highball, hurricane or other suitable glasses, straws, picks and garnish
Chopping boards and knives for fruit, trays, coasters and napkins
Cling film, labels and a marker; washing-up liquid, sanitiser and gloves
photos: Fruit washed and the work area set up
Fruit being cut safely on a clean board
Each drink being measured and made
The four finished drinks, garnished, in their glasses
A drink served from a tray, held by the base
Spare juice covered, labelled and dated in the fridge
The bar cleaned down, blender unplugged and washed
checklist: Washed hands and fruit before preparing any drink
Used a knife safely on a stable board, cutting away from the hand
Measured the ingredients and followed the recipe
Used the blender safely (lid on, switched off and unplugged before handling the blades)
Took ice only with the scoop
Chose a suitable glass and garnished the drink neatly
Served from a tray, from the guest's right, holding the glass by the base
Stored spare juice covered, labelled and dated, and cleaned the equipment
safety: Cut on a stable board with a sharp knife; carry knives point down and never try to catch a falling knife
Keep the blender lid on while it runs and unplug it before touching the blades
Use only the ice scoop in the ice bin; if a glass breaks near the ice, empty and clean the bin
Keep juice and milk at 5 °C or below, or as the Centre's food safety plan says
Wipe spills at once and put out a wet floor sign
